summary: Replace the heuristic layout with multi-start optimisation: SLSQP over centres and radii (maximise the sum of radii subject to pairwise non-overlap and wall constraints), seeded from random and ring-like starts, keeping the best feasible result within a time budget.

Added a basin-hopping phase: after about 40% of the time on multi-start, the program repeatedly perturbs the best solution (jitter, relocating a few circles, or swapping two) and re-optimises with SLSQP. It keeps a perturbed result only if it improves the sum of radii.

Phase 2 now uses Metropolis-style acceptance (a small, decaying temperature) so the search can leave a local optimum. It tracks the global best separately and resets to it after a run of rejected moves.

Phase 2 re-optimisations now include only circle pairs closer than 0.55, which shrinks the SLSQP constraint set. Each run is faster, so more basin-hopping moves fit in the time. Finalisation still checks every pair, and the total time budget goes up from 240 s to 270 s.
